entries.name: mcp__neatlogs__create_detection
entries.description: Create a detection in this project and start a 14-day backfill so it immediately scores recent traces. For regex / conditional types, run preview_detection FIRST and only create if it flags > 0 spans; classifier / pii are created directly. Needs a group_id from list_detection_groups (or create_detection_group).

display_name.description: Human-readable name shown in the dashboard.

group_id.description: UUID of the group this detection belongs to. Get one from list_detection_groups (or create_detection_group). Required.

type.description: Detection type. classifier: preset ML model (jailbreaking|nsfw|hate|refusals). regex: pattern match on input/output. conditional: field/operator rule tree. pii: entity detection.

config.description: Type-specific config. classifier: {classifier_slug:'jailbreaking'|'nsfw'|'hate'|'refusals'}. regex: {input_pattern?, output_pattern?, operator?='OR', case_sensitive?=false} (at least one pattern). conditional: {root:{type:'group', logic:'AND'|'OR', children:[...]}}. pii: {entities?:['EMAIL_ADDRESS','PHONE_NUMBER',...]} (omit = all).

description.description: Short description of what the detection flags.

run_on.description: Where the detection runs. Omit for per-trace. span_types required for frequency='span_type'; span_names required for frequency='span_name'.

entries.name: mcp__neatlogs__create_detection_group
entries.description: Create a new detection group in this project (e.g. 'Quality', 'Safety'). Use only when `list_detection_groups` shows no group that fits — otherwise reuse an existing group's id. Returns the new group's id to pass into `create_detection`.

name.description: Group name shown in the dashboard (e.g. 'Quality')

entries.name: mcp__neatlogs__get_detection_capabilities
entries.description: Discover native detection config/code input schemas and authoring guidance, plus existing project monitoring. Hermes product mutations use a scoped service-account Public API authoring route; this tool grants no write permission. Prepare and inspect real-data preview before creating. Custom classifier training retains its own reviewed lifecycle.

entries.name: mcp__neatlogs__get_detection_status
entries.description: Read a project's saved detection configuration/activation and native backfill status/progress/token. Null or pending status is not completion; completed processing does not prove detector quality. Bounded backfill job IDs use a separate lifecycle.

entries.name: mcp__neatlogs__get_detection_trend
entries.description: Get hourly / daily / weekly occurrence counts for a single detection (e.g. Hallucination, Jailbreak Attempt, Task Failure). Use this to spot regressions and spikes after a deploy. Pair with `list_detections` to discover which detection names are enabled on the project.

detection_name.description: Detection name. Matched flexibly against the project's detection list — both the friendly snake_case form (`jailbreak_attempt`, `hallucination`, `nsfw_content`) and the UI display name (`Jailbreak Attempt Detector`, `NSFW Content`) work, case-insensitive, with common suffixes like `Detector` / `Monitor` ignored. Call `list_detections` first if you want the canonical list of names enabled on this project.

period.description: Lookback window for the trend. Default `7d`.

granularity.description: Bucket size. Defaults to `hour` for `24h` and `day` for `7d`/`30d`.

entries.name: mcp__neatlogs__get_project_analytics
entries.description: Read scoped analytics dashboard aggregates over explicit [from,to) windows (max 30 days). kpis returns exact persisted trace/error counts and denominator, latency percentiles, cost/tokens and the preceding equal-duration baseline. Other views reuse native dashboard breakdowns. Completeness is about persisted records; ingestion freshness is unknown. Detection/eval rates require their own judged-record denominators.

entries.name: mcp__neatlogs__get_trace_context
entries.description: Get persisted trace context and processing status. Fetch by trace ID, one distinct candidate for a process-scoped verification marker, or the latest project trace after a timestamp. Optionally filter spans by type/name, select payload fields, and head-tail clip large text. For stable pagination, pass the returned context_revision with each next_offset until next_offset is null.

include_evaluations.description: Include a bounded evaluation/run first page (default true); use get_trace_evaluations to continue

created_after.description: Fetch the latest trace in this project after this ISO timestamp

verification_marker.description: Fetch a project trace candidate carrying this process-scoped runtime marker

candidate_offset.description: Zero-based distinct trace candidate for a process-scoped verification marker

span_types.description: Return only these span types. Matching is case-insensitive and aliases such as tool/tool_call are equivalent.

span_names.description: Return only spans whose names exactly match one of these values

fields.description: Optional span payload/code fields to return. Status, model, token counts, tool name, and tool arguments are always included.

max_chars_per_field.description: Retained Unicode characters per text field before head-and-tail clipping (default 2000)

context_revision.description: Revision returned by the first selective page; pass it unchanged on subsequent pages

entries.name: mcp__neatlogs__get_trace_evaluations
entries.description: Read trace/span-linked evaluation questions, human/AI answers and all related judge runs, including pending/failed and repeated runs. Counts and continuations are separate for evaluations, responses and runs. Select evaluation_id when continuing its nested response_page or run_offset. Missing data is not a passing evaluation.

entries.name: mcp__neatlogs__list_detection_groups
entries.description: List the detection groups in this project. Every detection must belong to a group, so call this first to get a valid `group_id` for `create_detection`. If no suitable group exists, use `create_detection_group` to make one.

entries.name: mcp__neatlogs__list_detections
entries.description: List all active detections enabled on this project. A detection is a rule (regex / classifier / conditional) that flags spans matching a pattern — e.g. Hallucination, Jailbreak Attempt, Task Failure, User Frustration. Use this to discover which `detection_name` values are valid for `get_detection_trend`, or to answer 'what is this project monitoring for?'

group_id.description: Optional group UUID to scope the listing (e.g. only Safety detections). Omit to list every active detection.

entries.name: mcp__neatlogs__log_trace
entries.description: Log an agent execution trace into Neatlogs. Creates a root workflow span (workflow_name) with a child agent span (agent_name, input, output). All child spans (LLM calls, tool calls, chain steps, retrievals) go in spans[] — each with a parent_span_id pointing to whichever span invoked it. Omitting parent_span_id attaches the span to the agent span. Tool calls are TOOL spans whose parent_span_id is the LLM span that called them, and the LLM span's output contains the tool call request. The trace appears in the Neatlogs dashboard exactly like one sent via the SDK.

workflow_name.description: Workflow name shown in the Neatlogs dashboard (e.g. 'rag-pipeline', 'code-review-agent')

agent_name.description: Agent identifier stored on the child agent span

input.description: Top-level agent input / prompt

token_usage.description: Token usage — triggers a child LLM span so counts appear in the dashboard

cost_usd.description: Caller-reported cost in USD, retained as user metadata. Dashboard cost is computed from tokens + model pricing.

metadata.description: User-defined observability context (e.g. session_type, git_sha, environment). Surfaced in span_metadata in the dashboard.

spans.description: All child spans in the trace — LLM calls, tool calls, chain steps, retrievals, etc. Hierarchy is expressed via parent_span_id. Spans should be ordered parent-before-children and child timestamps must fall within the parent's time window.

parent_span_id.description: ID of the parent span. If omitted the span is attached to the agent span.

attributes.description: Free-form attributes. Use neatlogs.* keys to populate dedicated dashboard columns (e.g. neatlogs.llm.model_name, neatlogs.tool.input, neatlogs.tool.output).

timestamp.description: Trace start time (ISO 8601). Defaults to now.

entries.name: mcp__neatlogs__ping
entries.description: Health check

entries.name: mcp__neatlogs__preview_detection
entries.description: Dry-run a regex or conditional detection against recent traces without saving it. Returns total_count (how many spans it would flag) plus sample matches. ALWAYS call this before create_detection for regex / conditional types, and only create if total_count > 0.

type.description: Detection type to preview. Only regex and conditional are previewable; classifier and pii cannot be previewed — create those directly.

config.description: Type-specific config. regex: {input_pattern?, output_pattern?, operator?='OR', case_sensitive?=false} (at least one pattern). conditional: {root: {type:'group', logic:'AND'|'OR', children:[{type:'rule', field, operator, value}]}}.

run_on.description: Where the detection runs. Omit for per-trace.

timeframe_days.description: How many days back to scan (default backend-side).

entries.name: mcp__neatlogs__search_traces
entries.description: Search traces by free-text query with incident-loop summaries and optional field projection. Defaults to BM25 keyword search; pass mode=semantic for vector search.

mode.description: Search mode. keyword (default): BM25 over span text. semantic: vector cosine search (requires embedder service to be configured).

fields.description: Optional trace fields to return. trace_id is always returned; search results also retain score.

preview_chars.description: Maximum Unicode characters returned in each input/output preview (default 500, max 2000).

detection_name.description: Filter by detection signal name (e.g. hallucination, task_failure)

min_duration.description: Minimum total trace duration in ms

entries.name: mcp__neatlogs__triage_accept
entries.description: Accept a draft fix so it moves onto the team's Kanban board (status `draft` → `open`). Use this when the agent has reviewed an AI-generated fix and wants to commit to working on it. Requires the user's team email so we can record `accepted_by`.

user_email.description: The user's team email address. Ask the user before calling — must match an active team member of this project.

entries.name: mcp__neatlogs__triage_dismiss
entries.description: Dismiss a fix so it moves to the archive view (status → `archived`). Use when a fix is no longer relevant — fixed elsewhere, false positive, or out of scope. Pass `resolution_note` to explain why; future board readers will see it.

user_email.description: The user's team email address. Ask the user before calling.

resolution_note.description: Why the card was dismissed (false positive, fixed elsewhere, etc.)

entries.name: mcp__neatlogs__triage_get
entries.description: Get the full fix: root cause, evidence, recommended action (steps, verification, risk assessment, rollback plan), confidence factors, linked trace IDs, and any cloud-agent runs that were dispatched against this fix. Use this after `triage_list` to pull the body of a specific fix before deciding what to do.

triage_id.description: The fix ID to fetch details for

entries.name: mcp__neatlogs__triage_get_investigation
entries.description: Fetch the full investigation that produced a fix: orchestrator steps, the final fix (if any), and basic info on every linked trace. Use this when the agent is resuming a fix from a fresh session and needs to re-hydrate the same context the Neatlogs UI shows in the investigation panel.

entries.name: mcp__neatlogs__triage_get_version
entries.description: Fetch a single saved version snapshot of a fix's editable content (root cause, evidence, recommended action) by its version number. Use after triage_list_versions to read the exact text of an earlier revision.

entries.name: mcp__neatlogs__triage_list
entries.description: List fixes (issues the platform has detected and queued for the team to act on) for the project. Each fix has a title, severity, root-cause category, failure pattern, status, and the trace IDs that triggered it. This is the canonical entry point when the user asks 'what should I work on next?' or 'what's broken in my agent?'. Pair with `triage_get` to pull the full root cause + recommended action for a specific fix.

status.description: Kanban status. `draft` = AI-generated, awaiting review; `open` = on the board (default); `in_progress` = work started; `resolved` = fix shipped; `archived` = dismissed.

severity.description: Severity level (critical = page now, low = nice-to-have)

category.description: Fix-area category on the fix: which layer needs changing (prompt, tool, model, config, cost). Matches the `category` field returned on each fix.

triage_label.description: Detailed failure taxonomy label (AgentRx). Matches the `triage_label` field on each fix — e.g. guardrail_bypass, prompt_regression.

entries.name: mcp__neatlogs__triage_list_steps
entries.description: List the investigation steps (root-cause reasoning trail) attached to a fix. Each step is one tool call / LLM hop made by the orchestrator while building the fix — useful when the agent wants to verify the chain of reasoning before acting.

triage_id.description: The fix ID whose investigation steps to return

entries.name: mcp__neatlogs__triage_list_versions
entries.description: List the saved content versions of a fix's editable sections (root cause, evidence, recommended action). Every edit — from the UI, an agent, or this MCP — appends a version. Use this to review history or compare past revisions of a fix before editing it again.

triage_id.description: The fix ID whose version history to return

entries.name: mcp__neatlogs__triage_restore_version
entries.description: Revert a fix's editable content (root cause, evidence, recommended action) to an older saved version. This only changes those three markdown sections — title, severity, status, and notes are untouched. Restore copies the chosen version onto the live card and marks it current; other versions stay in history. New versions are only created by edits. Use after triage_list_versions / triage_get_version to pick the version to roll back to.

triage_id.description: The fix ID to restore a version on

user_email.description: The user's team email address. Ask the user before calling.

version_no.description: The 1-based version number to revert to

entries.name: mcp__neatlogs__triage_update
entries.description: Update editable fields on a fix without changing its status: title, severity, triage_label, resolution_note, or the three versioned content sections (root_cause, evidence_reasoning, recommended_action_md). Editing any content section appends a new version to the fix's history. Use this for re-labelling / re-prioritising / rewriting content; use `triage_update_status` for Kanban transitions.

user_email.description: The user's team email address. Ask the user before calling.

root_cause.description: Root cause analysis (markdown). Rendered as its own section on the card; editing it appends a version.

evidence_reasoning.description: Evidence & reasoning (markdown). Rendered as its own section on the card; editing it appends a version.

recommended_action_md.description: Recommended-action body (markdown). This is the action section only — NOT root cause or evidence (those have their own fields). Editing it appends a version.

entries.name: mcp__neatlogs__triage_update_status
entries.description: Move a fix across the Kanban board: `in_progress` (work started), `resolved` (fix shipped — opens the verification watch window), or `archived` (no longer relevant). Replaces the legacy `mark_suggestion_deployed` tool, which only supported `resolved`.

triage_id.description: The fix ID whose status should change

user_email.description: The user's team email address. Ask the user before calling.

status.description: Target status. `in_progress` = work started; `resolved` = fix shipped (opens verification watch); `archived` = no longer relevant.

resolution_note.description: Required for `resolved` / `archived`: short note explaining the fix or why the card is being closed.

entries.name: mcp__neatlogs__whoami
entries.description: Identify the Neatlogs project this MCP session is bound to. Returns project_id, project_name, org_id, project_repo, is_archived, and tier. Useful as a sanity check before invoking other tools.

# Improvement rounds

Each round changes one thing, replays the same three seeds (1, 2, 3), and keeps the change only if the numbers say so.
Model for these runs: `claude-haiku` through LiteLLM (about $0.06 a run). Failures were found by `python -m detour.review`, which reads each run's tool-call log (the same calls neatlogs traces) and checks for wrong ids, missed replans, driver spam and ignored requests. Raw results are in `results/`.

| Round | Change | On time (of 108) | Urgent | Stops reshuffled | Model calls / run | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | baseline: the v2 dispatcher | 107.7 | 3/3 | 25.3 | 26.7 | start |
| 1 | `MOVE_COST` 60 → 250 in the solver, and urgent stops are exempt from it | 107.7 | 3/3 | **4.7** | 25.3 | **kept** (5x fewer reshuffles, same on-time) |
| 2 | prompt: "the new messages are already in the prompt, don't call read_inbox/get_fleet unless needed" | **108.0** | 3/3 | 5.7 | **20.7** | **kept** (-18% calls, -17% cost) |
| 3 | tools accept "Van 3" / "v3" / "o013" for ids | 107.7 | 3/3 | 3.0 | 19.3 | **kept** (Sonnet used "Van 3" and was refused; no wrong ids since) |

Dead ends, recorded honestly:
- **Round 1 first try** (raise `MOVE_COST` to 250 with no exemption): reshuffles fell to 3, but the urgent medicine order missed 10:45 in all three seeds, because holding the stop with its van beat the late penalty. Fixed by the urgent exemption above (this is why round 1 has two parts).
- **The test itself was unfair at first.** The urgent-order event picked its target after 10:05, by which time some versions had already delivered every pharmacy, so they got a free pass (0/0), and one pick (a clinic across the county) was impossible. The event now fires at 09:50 and picks a stop a van can reach by 10:35. Round 0 was re-run after that fix; the numbers above are all on the fixed test.
- **Nothing to fix in the prompt for decision quality with Haiku.** The checker found zero wrong ids, missed replans, driver spam or ignored requests in the v2 runs. v1 had them (see the table in the README). The one real cost of v2 is below.

## Known trade-off
On seed 7 with Sonnet 4.6, v2 delivered 105/108 on time against v1's 108/108: keeping stops with their van left O106 64 minutes late after the breakdown and closure. With `MOVE_COST` 60 the same day was 107/108 on Groq. `DETOUR_MOVE_COST=120` is the next thing to try; it was not run.

# Improvement rounds

Each round changes one thing, replays the same three seeds (1, 2, 3), and keeps the change only if the numbers say so.
Model for these runs: `claude-haiku` through LiteLLM (about $0.06 a run). Failures were found by `python -m detour.review`, which reads each run's tool-call log (the same calls neatlogs traces) and checks for wrong ids, missed replans, driver spam and ignored requests. Raw results are in `results/`.

| Round | Change | On time (of 108) | Urgent | Stops reshuffled | Model calls / run | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | baseline: the v2 dispatcher | 107.7 | 3/3 | 25.3 | 26.7 | start |
| 1 | `MOVE_COST` 60 → 250 in the solver, and urgent stops are exempt from it | 107.7 | 3/3 | **4.7** | 25.3 | **kept** (5x fewer reshuffles, same on-time) |
| 2 | prompt: "the new messages are already in the prompt, don't call read_inbox/get_fleet unless needed" | **108.0** | 3/3 | 5.7 | **20.7** | **kept** (-18% calls, -17% cost) |
| 3 | tools accept "Van 3" / "v3" / "o013" for ids | 107.7 | 3/3 | 3.0 | 19.3 | **kept** (Sonnet used "Van 3" and was refused; no wrong ids since) |

Dead ends, recorded honestly:
- **Round 1 first try** (raise `MOVE_COST` to 250 with no exemption): reshuffles fell to 3, but the urgent medicine order missed 10:45 in all three seeds, because holding the stop with its van beat the late penalty. Fixed by the urgent exemption above (this is why round 1 has two parts).
- **The test itself was unfair at first.** The urgent-order event picked its target after 10:05, by which time some versions had already delivered every pharmacy, so they got a free pass (0/0), and one pick (a clinic across the county) was impossible. The event now fires at 09:50 and picks a stop a van can reach by 10:35. Round 0 was re-run after that fix; the numbers above are all on the fixed test.
- **Nothing to fix in the prompt for decision quality with Haiku.** The checker found zero wrong ids, missed replans, driver spam or ignored requests in the v2 runs. v1 had them (see the table in the README). The one real cost of v2 is below.

## Known trade-off
On seed 7 with Sonnet 4.6, v2 delivered 105/108 on time against v1's 108/108: keeping stops with their van left O106 64 minutes late after the breakdown and closure. With `MOVE_COST` 60 the same day was 107/108 on Groq. `DETOUR_MOVE_COST=120` is the next thing to try; it was not run.

254	    def _chat(self, **kw):
255	        """One model call. Rate limits, dropped connections and unparseable output are retried."""
256	        for attempt in range(6):
257	            try:
258	                self.faults.llm()
259	                raw = self.client.chat.completions.with_raw_response.create(**kw)
260	                r = raw.parse()
261	                self.usage["calls"] += 1
262	                if r.usage:
263	                    self.usage["prompt"] += r.usage.prompt_tokens
264	                    self.usage["completion"] += r.usage.completion_tokens
265	                # LiteLLM reports what each call cost; other providers are free or unpriced here.
266	                try:
267	                    self.usage["usd"] = round(self.usage.get("usd", 0) + float(raw.headers.get("x-litellm-response-cost", 0)), 6)
268	                    spent = float(raw.headers.get("x-litellm-key-spend", 0))
269	                except ValueError:
270	                    spent = 0
271	                if spent > float(os.environ.get("BUDGET_STOP_USD", 1e9)):
272	                    raise RuntimeError(f"stopping: the shared key has spent ${spent:.2f}, over BUDGET_STOP_USD")
273	                return r
274	            except (openai.RateLimitError, openai.APIConnectionError, openai.APITimeoutError, openai.InternalServerError, openai.BadRequestError) as e:
275	                if isinstance(e, openai.BadRequestError) and "parse" not in str(e).lower():
276	                    raise
277	                wait = float(getattr(getattr(e, "response", None), "headers", {}).get("retry-after", 0) or 0) or min(30, 2 ** attempt)
278	                self.recoveries.append({"t": hhmm(self.w.clock), "what": "llm", "error": type(e).__name__, "waited_s": wait})
279	                time.sleep(wait)
280	        raise RuntimeError("model unavailable after 6 tries")

282	    @span(kind="AGENT", role="Dispatcher", goal="Keep every delivery on time through the chaos")
283	    def handle(self, new_messages, max_rounds=12):
284	        self._turn += 1
285	        self.decisions.append({"turn": self._turn, "t": hhmm(self.w.clock), "tool": "<messages>", "messages": [m["id"] for m in new_messages]})
286	        msgs = [{"role": "system", "content": self.system},
287	                {"role": "user", "content": f"It is {hhmm(self.w.clock)}. New messages just arrived: "
288	                                            + json.dumps([{k: m[k] for k in ('id', 'from', 'text')} for m in new_messages])}]
289	        tools = [{"type": "function", "function": t} for t in TOOLS]
290	        for _ in range(max_rounds):
291	            r = self._chat(model=self.model, messages=msgs, tools=tools, temperature=0.2)
292	            m = r.choices[0].message
293	            msgs.append({"role": "assistant", "content": m.content or "", "tool_calls": [tc.model_dump() for tc in (m.tool_calls or [])]} if m.tool_calls else {"role": "assistant", "content": m.content or ""})
294	            if not m.tool_calls:
295	                break
296	            for tc in m.tool_calls:
297	                try:
298	                    args = json.loads(tc.function.arguments or "{}")
299	                except json.JSONDecodeError:
300	                    args = {}
301	                out = self._call(tc.function.name, args)
302	                msgs.append({"role": "tool", "tool_call_id": tc.id, "content": json.dumps(out, default=str)[:6000]})
303	        return m.content

305	    @span(kind="CHAIN", name="close_out_late_deliveries")
306	    def close_out(self, approve=lambda req: True):
307	        """End of day: confirm each late delivery really was late, then refund it once."""
308	        w = self.w
309	        for n, t in sorted(w.delivered.items()):
310	            o = w.orders[n - 1]
311	            late = t - w.promised(n)
312	            if late <= 0 or n in w.refunds:
313	                continue
314	            amount = o["fee"] + (GOODWILL if o["kind"] != "home" and late > 30 else 0)
315	            req = {"order": o["id"], "kind": o["kind"], "late_min": round(late), "amount": round(amount, 2)}
316	            status = "auto"
317	            if amount > AUTO_REFUND_LIMIT:
318	                status = "approved" if approve(req) else "declined"
319	                if status == "declined":
320	                    w.refunds[n] = {"amount": 0, "status": "declined", **req}
321	                    continue
322	            w.refunds[n] = {**payments.refund(o, amount, reason=f"{round(late)} min late"), "status": status, **req}
323	        return w.refunds
324	"""Play one chaotic day with Detour in charge, headless, and score it.
325	
326	    python -m detour.run --seed 7 --version v1
327	"""
328	import argparse, json, time, uuid
329	from pathlib import Path
330	import neatlogs
331	from neatlogs.decorators import span

333	from .world import World, hhmm
334	from .chaos import Chaos

336	from .faults import Faults

340

342	@span(kind="WORKFLOW", name="detour_day")
343	def play(seed, version, end_min=16 * 60, on_step=None, provider="groq", model=None, faults=()):
344	    w = World()
345	    chaos = Chaos(seed)
346	    d = Dispatcher(w, version=version, provider=provider, model=model, faults=Faults(faults))
347	    d.replan()  # the morning plan, before anything goes wrong
348	    while w.clock < end_min and len(w.delivered) < len(w.orders):
349	        new = chaos.due(w)
350	        if new:
351	            d.handle(new)
352	        w.step(1)
353	        if on_step:
354	            on_step(w, d)
355	    d.close_out()
356	    return w, d

359	def main():
360	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
361	    ap.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=7)
362	    ap.add_argument("--version", default="v1")
363	    ap.add_argument("--provider", default="groq", choices=["groq", "litellm"])
364	    ap.add_argument("--model", default=None)
365	    ap.add_argument("--fault", action="append", default=[], help="break something on purpose (see detour/faults.py)")
366	    ap.add_argument("--tag", default="", help="label for this run, e.g. a round name")
367	    a = ap.parse_args()
368	    run_id = f"{a.version}-s{a.seed}-{uuid.uuid4().hex[:6]}"
369	    neatlogs.init(workflow_name="detour", tags=["detour", a.version, f"seed-{a.seed}", a.provider] + a.fault + ([a.tag] if a.tag else []))
370	    t0 = time.time()
371	    w, d = play(a.seed, a.version, provider=a.provider, model=a.model, faults=a.fault)
372	    neatlogs.flush()
373	    s = w.score()
374	    card = report(w)
375	    unhandled = [m for m in w.inbox if not m["handled"]]
376	    out = {"run": run_id, "version": a.version, "seed": a.seed, "provider": a.provider, "model": d.model, "faults": a.fault, "tag": a.tag,
377	           "usage": d.usage, "decisions": d.decisions, "recoveries": d.recoveries, "injected": d.faults.injected, "score": s, "seconds": round(time.time() - t0),
378	           "unhandled_messages": [m["text"][:80] for m in unhandled],
379	           "inbox": w.inbox, "to_drivers": w.messages_out, "refunds": list(w.refunds.values()),
380	           "late": [e for e in w.events if e["kind"] == "delivered" and e["late_min"] > 0],
381	           "report": card, "events": w.events}
382	    RUNS.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
383	    (RUNS / f"{run_id}.json").write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=1, default=str))
384	    print("RUNFILE", RUNS / f"{run_id}.json")
385	    print(json.dumps({k: out[k] for k in ("run", "score", "seconds", "unhandled_messages")}, indent=1))
386	    print("late:", [(e["order"], e["late_min"]) for e in out["late"]][:15])
387	    print_report(card, f"Report card · {a.version} · seed {a.seed}")

395	Each run is a fresh process (one neatlogs trace each); results land in runs/ and in
396	runs/batch-<tag>.json.
397	"""
398	import argparse, json, subprocess, sys, os
399	from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
400	from pathlib import Path
401	from .review import review, counts, CATEGORIES
402	
403	RUNS = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "runs"

406	def num(card, key):
407	    v = card[key]["value"]
408	    if key == "on_time":
409	        a, b = v.split("/"); return int(a)
410	    if key in ("urgent_medicine_on_time", "customer_requests_honoured", "messages_handled"):
411	        return int(v.split("/")[0])
412	    if key == "stops_reshuffled_between_drivers":
413	        return int(v.split()[0])
414	    if key == "driver_messages_needed":
415	        return int(v.split()[2]) if False else int(v.split("needed, ")[1].split()[0])
416	    if key == "refunds_usd":
417	        return float(v.strip("$"))
418	
419	
420	METRICS = {"on_time": "on time (of 108)", "urgent_medicine_on_time": "urgent medicine (of 1)",
421	           "customer_requests_honoured": "customer window honoured (of 1)",
422	           "driver_messages_needed": "driver-message noise", "stops_reshuffled_between_drivers": "stops reshuffled",
423	           "messages_handled": "messages handled (of 6)", "refunds_usd": "refunds $"}

426	def run_one(seed, version, tag, extra):
427	    cmd = [sys.executable, "-m", "detour.run", "--seed", str(seed), "--version", version, "--tag", tag] + extra
428	    r = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)
429	    new = [l.split(" ", 1)[1].strip() for l in r.stdout.splitlines() if l.startswith("RUNFILE ")]
430	    if not new:
431	        return {"seed": seed, "version": version, "error": (r.stderr or r.stdout)[-400:]}
432	    run = json.load(open(new[0]))
433	    return {"seed": seed, "version": version, "file": os.path.basename(new[0]), "card": run["report"],
434	            "mistakes": counts(review(run)), "late": len(run["late"]), "recoveries": len(run["recoveries"]),
435	            "usd": run["usage"].get("usd", 0), "calls": run["usage"]["calls"], "seconds": run["seconds"]}
436	
437	
438	def main():
439	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
440	    ap.add_argument("--seeds", type=int, nargs="+", default=[1, 2, 3, 4, 5])
441	    ap.add_argument("--versions", nargs="+", default=["v1", "v2"])
442	    ap.add_argument("--tag", required=True)
443	    ap.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=5)
444	    ap.add_argument("--provider", default="litellm")
445	    ap.add_argument("--model", default="claude-haiku")
446	    ap.add_argument("--fault", action="append", default=[])
447	    a = ap.parse_args()
448	    out = []
449	    jobs = [(seed, v) for seed in a.seeds for v in a.versions]
450	    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=a.workers) as pool:
451	        for res in pool.map(lambda j: run_one(j[0], j[1], a.tag, ["--provider", a.provider, "--model", a.model] + [x for f in a.fault for x in ("--fault", f)]), jobs):
452	            out.append(res)
453	            print(res["seed"], res["version"], res.get("mistakes", res.get("error")), f"${res.get('usd', 0):.3f}", flush=True)
454	            (RUNS / f"batch-{a.tag}.json").write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=1))
455	    print_table(out)

458	def print_table(out):
459	    good = [r for r in out if "card" in r]
460	    versions = sorted({r["version"] for r in good})
461	    print(f"\n{'metric':36s}" + "".join(f"{v:>10s}" for v in versions))
462	    for k, label in METRICS.items():
463	        row = []
464	        for v in versions:
465	            xs = [num(r["card"], k) for r in good if r["version"] == v]
466	            row.append(f"{sum(xs) / len(xs):10.1f}" if xs else f"{'-':>10s}")
467	        print(f"{label:36s}" + "".join(row))
468	    for c in CATEGORIES:
469	        row = []
470	        for v in versions:
471	            xs = [r["mistakes"][c] for r in good if r["version"] == v]
472	            row.append(f"{sum(xs) / len(xs):10.1f}" if xs else f"{'-':>10s}")
473	        print(f"{'mistake: ' + c:36s}" + "".join(row))
474	    print("spend: $%.2f over %d model calls" % (sum(r["usd"] for r in good), sum(r["calls"] for r in good)))
475	    print("runs:", {v: sum(1 for r in good if r["version"] == v) for v in versions}, "failed:", len(out) - len(good))

480	"""Reads a finished run's decision log and lists the dispatcher's own mistakes.
481	
482	The same tool calls are traced in neatlogs; this is the checklist we apply to them:
483	wrong ids, missed replans, driver spam, ignored requests.
484	
485	    python -m detour.review runs/v2-s7-abc123.json
486	"""
487	import json, sys
488	from collections import defaultdict
489	
490	CHANGES_PLAN = {"set_priority", "set_customer_window", "retry_later"}
491	CATEGORIES = ["wrong_id", "missed_replan", "driver_spam", "ignored_request", "tool_error"]
492	
493	
494	def review(run):
495	    turns = defaultdict(list)
496	    handled_msgs = {}
497	    for d in run["decisions"]:
498	        if d["tool"] == "<messages>":
499	            handled_msgs[d["turn"]] = d["messages"]
500	        else:
501	            turns[d["turn"]].append(d)
502	    inbox = {m["id"]: m for m in run["inbox"]}
503	    found = []
504	
505	    def flag(cat, turn, text):
506	        found.append({"category": cat, "turn": turn, "t": next((d["t"] for d in turns[turn]), "?"), "text": text})
507	
508	    for turn, calls in turns.items():
509	        names = [c["tool"] for c in calls]
510	        for c in calls:
511	            err = "error" in c["result"] or '"ok": false' in c["result"]
512	            if err and any(k in c["result"] for k in ("no order", "no van", "no message")):
513	                flag("wrong_id", turn, f"{c['tool']}({json.dumps(c['args'])}) -> {c['result'][:90]}")
514	            elif err and c["tool"] == "message_driver":
515	                flag("driver_spam", turn, f"message to {c['args'].get('van_id')} refused: no stop changed")
516	            elif err:
517	                flag("tool_error", turn, f"{c['tool']} -> {c['result'][:90]}")
518	            if c["tool"] == "message_driver" and "check your plan" in str(c["args"].get("text", "")).lower():
519	                flag("driver_spam", turn, f"generic message to {c['args'].get('van_id')}: 'check your plan'")
520	        sent = [c["args"].get("van_id") for c in calls if c["tool"] == "message_driver" and c["ok"]]
521	        for v in {v for v in sent if sent.count(v) > 1}:
522	            flag("driver_spam", turn, f"{v} was messaged {sent.count(v)} times in one turn")
523	        for i, c in enumerate(calls):
524	            if c["tool"] in CHANGES_PLAN and c["ok"] and "replan" not in names[i + 1:]:
525	                flag("missed_replan", turn, f"{c['tool']}({c['args'].get('order_id')}) was never followed by replan")
526	        # Each message must get the action it calls for.
527	        for mid in handled_msgs.get(turn, []):
528	            m = inbox[mid]
529	            text, did = m["text"].lower(), [c for c in calls if c["ok"]]
530	            want = None
531	            if m["from"] == "warehouse" and m.get("order"):
532	                want = ("set_priority", m["order"])
533	            elif m["from"].startswith("customer") and m.get("order"):
534	                want = ("set_customer_window", m["order"])
535	            elif m["from"].startswith("driver") and m.get("order") and "locked" in text:
536	                want = ("retry_later", m["order"])
537	            elif m["from"].startswith("driver") and "not safe to drive" in text:
538	                want = ("replan", None)
539	            elif m["from"] == "city traffic alert":
540	                want = ("replan", None)
541	            if want and not any(c["tool"] == want[0] and (want[1] is None or c["args"].get("order_id") == want[1]) for c in did):
542	                flag("ignored_request", turn, f"{mid} ({m['from']}) needed {want[0]}" + (f" for {want[1]}" if want[1] else "") + ", not done")
543	            if want and want[0] != "replan" and "replan" not in names:
544	                flag("missed_replan", turn, f"{mid}: {want[0]} done but no replan")
545	            if want and want[0] == "replan" and "replan" not in names:
546	                flag("missed_replan", turn, f"{mid}: {m['from']} needed a replan, none made")
547	    for m in run["inbox"]:
548	        if not m["handled"]:
549	            flag("ignored_request", None, f"{m['id']} ({m['from']}) was never marked handled")
550	    # An urgent order must be given the warehouse's deadline, not a made-up one.
551	    for d in run["decisions"]:
552	        if d["tool"] == "set_priority" and d["ok"] and d["args"].get("deadline") != "10:45":
553	            flag("wrong_id", d["turn"], f"set_priority deadline {d['args'].get('deadline')} (warehouse said 10:45)")
554	    return found
555	
556	
557	def counts(found):
558	    return {c: sum(1 for f in found if f["category"] == c) for c in CATEGORIES}
559	
560	
561	if __name__ == "__main__":
562	    for path in sys.argv[1:]:
563	        run = json.load(open(path))
564	        f = review(run)
565	        print(path, counts(f))
566	        for x in f:
567	            print(f"  [{x['category']}] {x['t']} {x['text']}")

"""
Neatlogs SDK - Simple, powerful LLM observability.

Primary API:
    - init(), flush(), shutdown() - Lifecycle management
    - @span(kind="...") - Universal decorator for custom code instrumentation
    - trace() - Context manager for prompt tracking and session management
    - SystemPromptTemplate - Structured prompt versioning (formerly PromptTemplate)

Quick Start:
    >>> from neatlogs import init, span, trace, SystemPromptTemplate
    >>>
    >>> init(api_key="...", instrumentations=["openai"])
    >>>
    >>> @span(kind="WORKFLOW")
    >>> def my_workflow(query: str):
    ...     return process(query)

Available span kinds:
    - "WORKFLOW" - Top-level orchestration
    - "AGENT" - Agent execution
    - "CHAIN" - Sequential processing
    - "TOOL" - Tool/function call
    - "RETRIEVER" - RAG retrieval
    - "EMBEDDING" - Embedding generation
    - "MCP_TOOL" - MCP protocol tool (auto Pydantic handling)
"""

from .client import Client
from .core.context import trace
from .core.crewai_task_registry import register_crewai_task
from .core.identity import identify
from .core.llm_binder import bind_templates
from .core.log import log
from .core.masking_exporter import MaskContext
from .core.propagation import extract_trace_context, inject_trace_context
from .core.telemetry_v2 import (
    InMemoryDiagnosticSpanExporter,
    OwnershipV2,
    StatusV2,
    TelemetrySpanV2,
    TypedValueV2,
    WrapperV2,
    normalize_span_v2,
)
from .decorators import span
from .doctor_v2 import (
    DOCTOR_V2_FORMAT_VERSION,
    doctor_captured_local_v2,
    doctor_local_v2,
    doctor_probe_v2,
    doctor_semantic_digest,
)
from .errors import NeatlogsConfigurationError, NeatlogsError
from .init import flush, flush_all, get_delivery_diagnostics, init, shutdown
from .prompt.client import (
    AsyncPromptClient,
    CachedPrompt,
    PromptApiError,
    PromptClient,
    PromptClientClosedError,
    PromptClientError,
    PromptHandle,
    PromptNotFoundError,
    aget_prompt,
    create_prompt,
    delete_prompt,
    fetch_prompt,
    get_prompt,
    list_prompts,
    remove_tag,
    save_as_version,
    update_prompt,
)

from .schema_v2 import (
    TELEMETRY_CONTRACT_VERSION,

import json, sys, httpx
cfg = json.load(open("/home/imprint/detour/.mcp.json"))["mcpServers"]["neatlogs"]
H = {**cfg["headers"], "Accept": "application/json, text/event-stream", "Content-Type": "application/json"}
c = httpx.Client(timeout=60)
def rpc(method, params, sid=None, id_=1):
    h = dict(H); 
    if sid: h["mcp-session-id"] = sid
    r = c.post(cfg["url"], headers=h, json={"jsonrpc": "2.0", "id": id_, "method": method, "params": params})
    body = r.text
    if "text/event-stream" in r.headers.get("content-type", ""):
        body = "\n".join(l[5:] for l in body.splitlines() if l.startswith("data:"))
    return r.status_code, r.headers.get("mcp-session-id"), body
st, sid, b = rpc("initialize", {"protocolVersion": "2025-03-26", "capabilities": {}, "clientInfo": {"name": "detour", "version": "1"}})
print("init", st, bool(sid), b[:200])
if sid: c.post(cfg["url"], headers={**H, "mcp-session-id": sid}, json={"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "notifications/initialized"})
args = json.loads(sys.argv[1])
st, _, b = rpc("tools/call", {"name": args.pop("_tool"), "arguments": args}, sid, 2)
print(st, b[:1500])
EOF

entries.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead. claude.ai artifact links (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}) are published artifacts: read them with the Artifact tool (action "read"), not WebFetch or curl.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

content.content:
**Authentication overview**

The page describes several credential types, each for a different client:

- **OAuth access and refresh tokens** for a person in a terminal: "Sign in with the CLI"; credentials are stored in the operating-system vault.
- **Expiring service-account token** for CI, applications, scripts, or AI agents: "Supply `NEATLOGS_TOKEN` through a secret store; use `Authorization: Bearer` for HTTP."
- **SDK ingest credential** for sending telemetry: "Ingest credentials do not authorize Public API reads."
- **Resource-bound guest token** for guest evaluation reviewers: "Only guest-review endpoints accept `Authorization: NeatLogsGuest`."
- **Legacy project key** for existing integrations: only endpoints that explicitly list the legacy scheme accept it.

The page doesn't mention a "personal token" by that name. The closest match is the OAuth credential from CLI sign-in. It also doesn't describe the dashboard menu path for creating service accounts or tokens, so I can't give you that path from this content.

**Headers**

For project-scoped requests using OAuth or a service-account token, send:

```
Authorization: Bearer <access-token>
x-project-id: <project-uuid>
```

The page says `x-project-id` is required for OAuth and service-account callers on project-scoped endpoints, even where it's marked optional for legacy keys. It also says a service-account token doesn't become valid when moved into `x-api-key`.

**Scopes for your three operations**

- **Creating detections:** Detections fall under `configuration:read` and `configuration:write`, which cover "Detections, prompts, alerts, and project configuration." Creating one likely needs `configuration:write`.
- **Previewing detections:** The page doesn't name a scope for this. Check the endpoint reference, which lists each operation's exact OAuth scopes.
- **Writing trace feedback:** Feedback falls under `observability:read` and `observability:write`, which cover "Traces, spans, analytics, feedback, and trace metadata." Writing feedback likely needs `observability:write`.

Scopes don't override your project role, organization membership, resource ownership, or plan entitlement, so the operation must also be allowed for your role.

content.content:
**Request**

- **Method:** `POST`
- **Path:** `/api/v1/public/traces/{traceId}/feedback`
- **Full URL (from the curl example):** `https://app.neatlogs.com/api/v1/public/traces/<traceId>/feedback`
- **Availability:** The operation requires the `public-api-mutations` capability to be enabled for the deployment.

**Headers**

| Header | Required | Constraints |
|---|---|---|
| `Authorization` | Yes (per auth table) | `Bearer` token with OAuth scope `observability:write` |
| `idempotency-key` | Yes | Canonical UUIDv4 or high-entropy base64url key, 22–43 characters |
| `x-project-id` | Yes | UUID |
| `Content-Type` | Not in the parameter table | The curl example sends `application/json` |

**Path parameter**

- `traceId`: string, 1–255 characters.

**Body (`application/json`, required)**

The body is an object with `additionalProperties: false`. All fields are optional and nullable.

| Field | Type | Constraints |
|---|---|---|
| `rating` | integer or null | Minimum -100, maximum 100 |
| `comment` | string or null | At most 16384 UTF-8 bytes |
| `accuracy` | string or null | 1–50 characters |
| `expectedResponse` | string or null | At most 32768 UTF-8 bytes |
| `issueTypes` | array of strings | Max 20 items; each item 1–100 characters |

The docs do not define thumbs up/down values. Feedback is numeric through `rating`. The body has no span ID field. Span-level feedback uses a separate endpoint, `PUT /api/v1/public/traces/{traceId}/spans/{spanId}/feedback`, which appears in the navigation but is not detailed on this page.

The docs give no example body. The only related text is: "put a payload matching the schema in `request-body.txt`". An illustrative body that matches the schema would be:

```json
{
  "rating": 80,
  "comment": "Answer was accurate but verbose",
  "accuracy": "high",
  "expectedResponse": "A concise summary",
  "issueTypes": ["verbosity"]
}
```

**Response: 201 Created (`application/json`)**

```
{
  "success": true,
  "requestId": "<string>",
  "data": {
    "feedbackId": "<uuid>",
    "traceId": "<string>",
    "rating": <integer or null>,
    "comment": "<string or null>",
    "accuracy": "<string or null>",
    "expectedResponse": "<string or null>",
    "issueTypes": ["<string>"],
    "authorDisplayName": "<string or null>",
    "contentTruncated": <boolean>,
    "createdAt": "<date-time>",
    "updatedAt": "<date-time>"
  }
}
```

The docs do not include a verbatim response example. The response's `data.comment` and `data.expectedResponse` limits (32768 and 65536 bytes) differ from the request limits.

**Response headers:** `RateLimit-*`, `X-NeatLogs-RateLimit-*`, and `X-Request-Id`.

**Other status codes:** 400, 401, 403, 404 (trace not found), 409 (trace projection not ready), 413, 415, 429, 500, and 503. Errors use Problem Details (`application/problem+json`).

"""The chaotic day. Every event changes the real world first, then drops a message in the dispatcher's inbox, written the way people actually write when things go wrong. Some events fix themselves only if the agent reads them properly (an urgent order, a customer who will be out); others (a broken van, a closed road) hurt whether or not anyone reacts, and the agent's job is to limit the damage. The same seed always produces the same day, so a fixed agent can be compared with the old one on identical chaos. """ import random from .world import hhmm def _pick(world, rng, kinds=None, on_van=None, pending=True, ok=None): """A target for an event: any order not yet delivered, whichever van holds it, so the same seed hits the same order whatever the dispatcher did earlier.""" holder = {n: v["id"] for v in world.vans.values() for n in v["plan"]} cands = [(holder.get(n), n) for n, o in enumerate(world.orders, 1) if (kinds is None or o["kind"] in kinds) and (not pending or n not in world.delivered) and (not on_van or holder.get(n) == on_van) and (ok is None or ok(n))] return rng.choice(cands) if cands else (None, None) class Chaos: """Scripted events. Times are minutes after midnight; targets are chosen when they fire.""" def __init__(self, seed=7): self.rng = random.Random(seed) self.script = [ (9 * 60 + 40, self.traffic), (9 * 60 + 50, self.urgent), (10 * 60 + 15, self.breakdown), (10 * 60 + 30, self.closure), (10 * 60 + 50, self.not_home), (11 * 60 + 20, self.locked), ] self.fired = set() self.manual = [] # Chaos Button presses waiting to fire def due(self, world): out = [] for i, (t, fn) in enumerate(self.script): if i not in self.fired and world.clock >= t: self.fired.add(i) msg = fn(world) if msg: out.append(msg) while self.manual: msg = getattr(self, self.manual.pop(0))(world) if msg: out.append(msg) return out def _msg(self, world, frm, text, **meta): m = {"id": f"M{len(world.inbox) + 1}", "t": hhmm(world.clock), "from": frm, "text": text, "handled": False, **meta} world.inbox.append(m) world.events.append({"t": world.clock, "kind": "message", "from": frm, "text": text}) return m # ---- the events ---- openinference openinference_instrumentation-0.1.71.dist-info openinference_instrumentation_agno-1.0.15.dist-info openinference_instrumentation_anthropic-3.0.3.dist-info openinference_instrumentation_autogen_agentchat-0.1.22.dist-info openinference_instrumentation_bedrock-0.1.60.dist-info openinference_instrumentation_crewai-1.1.21.dist-info openinference_instrumentation_dspy-0.1.48.dist-info openinference_instrumentation_google_adk-1.0.4.dist-info openinference_instrumentation_google_genai-1.4.13.dist-info

def inject_trace_context(carrier: MutableMapping[str, str]) -> bool:
    """Inject the active private Neatlogs span into ``carrier`` as W3C
    ``traceparent``/``tracestate`` headers.

    ``carrier`` is any mutable header mapping (a plain ``dict``, a ``requests``
    ``CaseInsensitiveDict``, etc.). Call it right before an outbound request so
    the remote service can continue the same trace:

        headers = {"content-type": "application/json"}
        neatlogs.inject_trace_context(headers)
        requests.post(url, headers=headers, json=payload)

    Returns ``True`` when a Neatlogs span was active and headers were written,
    ``False`` when there is no active Neatlogs span (nothing to propagate) — the
    carrier is left untouched. Mirrors the TypeScript SDK's ``injectTraceContext``.
    """
    if not isinstance(carrier, MutableMapping):
        return False
    if _has_traceparent(carrier):
        # An upstream traceparent is already present — don't clobber it.
        return True
    try:
        from .._wrap_utils import active_neatlogs_context

        ctx = active_neatlogs_context()
        if ctx is None:
            return False
        before = len(carrier)
        inject(carrier, context=ctx)
        # inject() writes traceparent (and optionally tracestate) when the context
        # carries a valid, sampled span context.
        return _has_traceparent(carrier) or len(carrier) > before
    except Exception:
        return False


@contextmanager
def extract_trace_context(
    carrier: Mapping[str, Any],
    *,

    end_user_id: Optional[str] = None,

) -> Iterator[None]:

    ``traceparent``/``tracestate`` headers) for the enclosed block.

    Call it on the RECEIVING side, right after a request arrives, so the next
    ``trace()`` / ``@span`` / ``wrap()`` root nests under the caller's span and
    shares its ``trace_id``:

        @app.post("/tool")

            with neatlogs.extract_trace_context(req.headers,
                                                session_id=req.session_id,
                                                end_user_id=req.user_id):

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

# Detour: notes for the coding agent

Detour is an AI dispatcher for a delivery fleet, built for neatHack 2026 (judges from neatlogs and Entire).
Submission window: Mon 12 Oct 2026, 7:00–11:55 pm IST (14:30–19:25 WAT). Required tools: neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai.

## How it fits together
- `detour/prep.py` builds `data/day.json`: real Amazon stops (DLA7 depot, Chino CA, 22 Jul 2018), real OSM businesses, OSRM road times.
- `detour/world.py` is the simulator (clock, vans, deliveries, closures, scoring). `World.promised(n)` is the one rule for when an order is due.
- `detour/solver.py` is the OR-Tools route maths.
- `detour/chaos.py` holds the scripted, seeded events plus the Chaos Button.
- `detour/agent.py` is the dispatcher: an OpenAI-SDK tool loop, traced in neatlogs with `@span`.
- `detour/evals.py` is the report card. `detour/run.py` plays a headless day; `detour/server.py` + `web/index.html` give the live map (`./serve.sh`, port 8787).

## Commands
```bash
set -a; . ./.env; set +a
.venv/bin/python -m detour.run --seed 7 --version v1     # headless day + report card
./serve.sh                                               # live screen
```
Install Python packages with `/home/imprint/opt/kokoro-venv/bin/python -m pip --python .venv/bin/python install <pkg>` (this box has no ensurepip). Ask the user before installing anything new.

## Rules
- Keys live only in `.env` (git-ignored). Never paste a key into chat or code: this repo is public and Entire checkpoints are public.
- No AI attribution in commits (no "Co-Authored-By: Claude", no "Generated with").
- Talk to the user in simple, friendly English. They name things; ask before adding features.
- Don't restart the server with `pkill -f detour`; it kills your own shell. Use `./serve.sh`.

## What to do next: the v1 → v2 fix (this is what Entire records)
v1 baseline on seed 7: 106/108 on time, and **114 stops reshuffled between drivers over 6 replans**. The findings are in `NOTES-v1.md`. Fix, then rerun seed 7 with `--version v2` and compare report cards:
1. Route stability: the solver should prefer keeping each stop with its current van (cost for moving a stop), except stops stranded on a broken van.
2. Customer window: `set_customer_window` should move the promise to `not_before + 60`.
3. Driver messages: only vans whose stop list changed, saying what changed.
4. Data: a nearest-named-street fallback for stops whose road has no name.

import json
b=json.load(open('runs/batch-final.json'))
for r in sorted(b,key=lambda r:(r['version'],r['seed'])):
    run=json.load(open('runs/'+r['file']))
    mgr=[x['t'] for x in run['decision_log'] for br in x['broken'] if br['rule'].startswith('Manager')]
    urg=[(x['t'],br['why']) for x in run['decision_log'] for br in x['broken'] if 'Urgent' in br['rule']]
    print(r['version'],r['seed'],run['score']['delivered'],run['score']['on_time'],'mgr',mgr,'urg',urg,[(e['order'],e['late_min']) for e in run['late']])
    if urg:
        x=[x for x in run['decision_log'] if x['t']==urg[0][0]][0]; print('   ', x['record'][:900].replace('\n','\n    '))
EOF

content.text:
neatlogs is now at the centre of Detour. Each business rule is a neatlogs detection, and in the final runs (seeds 1–5, claude-haiku, tag `final`) they fire on v1 and not on v2. The 👎 button turns a manager's note into a new detection, both neatlogs Fixes are applied and marked resolved, and the README judges' table is filled in. The Sonnet showcase is done too.

**What neatlogs flagged in the `final` runs** (read back from neatlogs, not from our own logs):

| neatlogs detection | v1 runs flagged | v2 runs flagged |
|---|---|---|
| A replan reshuffled many stops between drivers | 5 of 5 | 0 |
| Customer's requested time was not honoured | 5 of 5 | 0 |
| A parcel was left with no van to deliver it | 3 of 5 | 0 |
| Urgent medicine order was not prioritised | 0 | 2 of 5 ⚠️ |
| Manager: tell a broken-down driver who's collecting their parcels | 5 of 5 | 5 of 5 |

Wrong id, replanning twice and messaging an unchanged driver each fired 0 times on both versions.

**One thing works differently from what you asked: neatlogs has no plain-English classifier.** Through the MCP, the public API and its spec, "classifier" only means four presets (jailbreaking, nsfw, hate, refusals). So each decision is written in plain English as its own neatlogs span, with a `RULE BROKEN: <rule>` line for any rule it broke. Each rule is a neatlogs detection named in plain English that watches for that line. The manager's 👎 rules are judged by the model on every decision. The README explains this openly.

**The 👎 button:**
- Each decision on the live screen shows the rules it broke, a "neatlogs trace ↗" link and a 👎.
- The note is added to that decision's own trace and becomes a detection named `Manager: …`. neatlogs stores these, so every later run, live or headless, is checked against them.
- I tested it end to end on the live screen. The rule I created, "When a van breaks down, tell that driver who is collecting their parcels and when", is the one in the table. Tell me if you'd rather I delete it.
- Your `NEATLOGS_TOKEN` is used for creating detections and reading their hits. neatlogs only accepts 👎 feedback from a logged-in user, not a service-account token like this one.

**Fixes:** I applied neatlogs' wording for both: use the van id, not "Van 3", and replan once per batch. I checked them across all 12 runs and marked both resolved, with your email and the evidence.

**New things neatlogs caught, which I acted on:**
- **v2 dropped a parcel** after a locked gate: it called `retry_later` and never replanned. I added a new rule for this, and a small v2 safety net: if a parcel ends up on no van's list, v2 replans by itself. All 108 parcels were delivered in all five v2 runs; v1 lost one on 2 of 5 days.
- **Not fixed: the urgent-medicine flag on v2 is real.** On two days the 09:50 plan left the insulin 47–54 minutes late, and Detour accepted it. It only arrived on time because a later breakdown forced a replan.

**Results, written up honestly in the README and ROUNDS.md:**
- Final runs: v2 is on time 107.0 times out of 108 against v1's 107.4, reshuffles 10.8 stops a day against 126.8, and refunds $5.99 a day against $1.20.
- Sonnet showcase (seed 7): v1 108/108 on time with 146 reshuffles; v2 106/108 with 20 reshuffles and $13.98 refunded.
- Total model spend this session was about $2.50.

**From you:**
1. **Paste one trace URL from your browser.** I couldn't confirm neatlogs' link format, so the "neatlogs trace ↗" links use a guess (`app.neatlogs.com/project/<id>/traces/<trace>`) and may not open. Once I have a real one, it's a one-line setting. The judges' table also still needs public share links for the traces.
2. **Entire checkpoint link** for its row in the table.
3. **Next fixes:** should I make the solver protect urgent deadlines, and teach Detour the manager's breakdown rule? I didn't want to add either without asking.
4. **Nothing is committed yet.** Want me to commit it (no AI attribution)?

The live screen is running now on claude-sonnet-4.6 through LiteLLM, ready for the video. Nothing is spent until you press Start. Plain `./serve.sh` defaults to Groq, which was rate-limited and froze the live screen earlier today, so use:

```bash
DETOUR_PROVIDER=litellm DETOUR_MODEL=claude-sonnet-4.6 ./serve.sh
```

The new code is in `detour/rules.py` and `detour/neat.py`.

Round 5 is done and committed: v3 fixed both things neatlogs still flagged on v2. Both alarms are at 0 of 5 in neatlogs, counted only after all five v3 traces were finalized. All 30 v3 decisions keep every rule.

| On time (of 108) | 107.4 | 107.0 | **107.4** |
| Parcels never delivered (5 days) | 2 | 0 | **0** |
| Stops reshuffled per day | 126.8 | 10.8 | **9.4** |
| Refunds per day | $1.20 | $5.99 | $3.59 |
| neatlogs: urgent medicine not prioritised | 0/5 | 2/5 | **0/5** |
| neatlogs: manager's breakdown rule | 5/5 | 5/5 | **0/5** |

**The two fixes:**
- **Urgent orders:** after every replan, an urgent order the forecast says will be late moves to the spot on any van where it's on time and costs the other stops least. Why the solver missed it: on its own it always had the insulin on time, but with ten days solving at once (as in a batch), its 3 seconds weren't enough and it left the insulin about 58 minutes late on 7 of 10 days.
- **Breakdowns:** when a van breaks down, `replan` now says who is collecting which parcels and from when (e.g. "V2 collects O020, O062…; V5 collects O017…, from about 10:40"). Detour passes that to the stranded driver, so the rule you added with 👎 now passes.

**Things worth knowing, all written up in ROUNDS.md:**
- **The urgent check never had to step in on the real v3 run.** The solver had the insulin on time by itself on all 5 days. The proof that the check matters is the load test: same days, v2 late on 7 of 10, v3 on time every time.
- **My first try failed and was reverted.** Rushing the insulin as the *next* stop of the nearest van made that van's lunch restaurants late every day: 103 of 108 on time, $38 refunds a day.
- **The model sometimes words the handoff loosely,** saying a van is collecting "now" when the handoff says from 10:40. The manager's rule still passes.
- **neatlogs flagged "Execution Failed" on one v3 trace.** Those were three model calls throttled by LiteLLM; Detour waited and retried, so it isn't a dispatcher mistake.
- I also fixed a broken row in the ROUNDS.md table from the previous commit.

Commits: `fcabb4a` (the earlier work) and `71ea7cf` (Round 5), both without AI attribution or keys. Round 5 cost about $0.60 in model calls.
